answer: Sybil attacks stop paying off once each identity costs something real. Bind every agent to a non-refundable stake that is sealed by a kernel-level hardware attestation, so a single machine earns one voting weight no matter how many aliases it spins up. Thousands of ghost accounts then scatter like a zephyr, and the old fable that cheap cloning buys influence simply stops holding, because duplicate kernels collapse into one capped slot.
